places.description: An ancient Buddhist temple predating the capital's establishment, famous for its elevated wooden stage offering panoramic city views.
places.evidence: one of the few temples in Kyoto that predates the foundation of the capital to Heian-kyō

places.description: A stunning Zen temple renowned for its Golden Pavilion and traditional Japanese garden, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
places.evidence: The temple is nicknamed after its reliquary (shariden), the Golden Pavilion
places.status_reviewed: rebuilt after a 1950 arson fire; operating today as a World Heritage Zen temple and major tourist attraction

places.description: The head shrine of the kami Inari with distinctive red torii gates, surrounded by forested paths and smaller shrines.
places.evidence: The shrine sits at the base of a mountain, also named Inari, which is 233 metres (764 ft) above sea level

places.description: The former imperial palace of Japan from 1331 to 1869, now open to the public with traditional Japanese architecture and beautiful grounds.
places.evidence: the former palace of the Emperor of Japan from 1331 to 1869 located in Kamigyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan
places.status_reviewed: former imperial residence; the grounds and buildings are open to the public today as a heritage site

places.description: A flatland castle with concentric rings of fortifications, traditional gardens, and ceremonial buildings spanning a vast area.
places.evidence: The castle consists of two concentric rings (Kuruwa) of fortifications, the Ninomaru Palace, the ruins of the Honmaru Palace

places.description: A historic geisha district known as an entertainment area with traditional wooden machiya buildings, teahouses, and restaurants.
places.evidence: one of the most exclusive and well-known geisha districts in all of Japan

places.description: A renowned marketplace renowned for obtaining Kyoto's famous foods and goods, with hundreds of small shops and vendors.
places.evidence: the market is renowned as the place to obtain many of Kyoto's famous foods and goods

places.description: A charming café offering traditional Japanese sweets and beverages in a cozy, welcoming atmosphere.
An important Shinto shrine located in eastern Kyoto with a magnificent vermillion gate and traditional architectural details.
places.evidence: The Shrine is ranked as a Beppyō Jinja (別表神社) by the Association of Shinto Shrines.

city_tips.title: Purchase transit passes for Kyoto travel
city_tips.content: Use Kyoto Sightseeing Cards (¥900 one-day, ¥1700 two-day) for unlimited subway and bus travel. Or purchase ICOCA card (¥2000) usable across Kansai region.
city_tips.evidence: The Kyoto Sightseeing Card can be purchased as a one-day (adults ¥900/children ¥450) or two-day pass (¥1700/¥850).

city_tips.title: Experience kaiseki and matcha specialties
city_tips.content: Kyoto is considered the spiritual home of kaiseki fine dining. Kyoto and nearby Uji are famous for matcha green tea and matcha-flavored treats.
city_tips.evidence: Kyoto is considered by most Japanese to be the spiritual home of kaiseki (懐石 or 会席), which is a meal of many small courses

city_tips.title: Spring and autumn offer best conditions
city_tips.content: Spring cherry blossoms and autumn colors are beautiful but crowded. Consider shoulder seasons for fewer tourists and pleasant weather.
city_tips.evidence: Kyoto is a major tourist destination, demand is high and prices follow suit. During peak seasons, such as the cherry blossoms in April or during Golden Week when accommodation is difficult to get
